problems.issue: The characteristic retinal degeneration is inadequately represented: rod-cone dystrophy is absent from simulated true and reported phenotypes, while visual findings are largely nonspecific impairment or blindness. The gene-level R1 cohort may represent a different phenotype, and toddlers need not report nyctalopia, but these caveats do not explain omission of the underlying retinal disease.

Example records contain unexplained findings such as angina pectoris, hemoptysis and irregular sperm-tail morphology. These are inappropriate routine features for this predominantly pediatric cerebro-oculo-renal syndrome and would teach misleading disease associations.

Records are substantially denser than R1-train and include redundant intellectual-disability labels and multiple behavioral descriptors, diluting the characteristic neurologic, retinal and renal phenotype.

summary: The early age, balanced sex distribution, developmental impairment, cerebellar abnormalities and renal disease are plausible. Missing explicit retinal degeneration and unrelated findings make the simulated cohort clinically implausible.
